name: Hierarchical Brick-Map DDA
definition: A ray marching technique that replaces a dense voxel buffer with a sparse hierarchical structure (brick-map) to skip empty regions. It uses a top-level grid of cells (stride 8 voxels) to quickly identify occupied bricks, then descends into those bricks for fine-grained DDA. This reduces memory footprint and traversal time in sparse volumes like drone airspace (>99% empty).
summary: Hierarchical Brick-Map DDA is a ray traversal technique that uses a sparse, hierarchical structure to skip empty regions, reducing memory and traversal time for sparse volumetric data.
